purpose: Canonical unitary reconstruction of Control 22 (18 June 2026 complaint concerning the insolvency administration), Control 24 (separate 18 June 2026 judge-specific complaint), the PH122→CAM / DP 1041/2017 retracto module, and the recurring Acosta Matos beneficiary perimeter. Maximum-hypothesis scores are evidential ceilings for investigation, not probabilities of guilt, adjudications or findings of criminal responsibility.

control22.principalTarget: Francisco de Borja Rodríguez-Batllori Laffitte / insolvency administration
control22.principalProvisionalHypothesis: possible administración desleal / disloyal administration, subject to proof of every statutory element
control22.currentProceduralContext: The Por Derecho control record links this complaint family to DP 1956/2026; the latest controlled public status is provisional dismissal communicated 21 July 2026. The dismissal is not represented as a final merits adjudication.

control24.principalTarget: Alberto López Villarrubia / judge-specific judicial-conduct route
control24.source: 02_Paquete_Unificado_Para_Presentacion_JUEZ_FINAL_17JUNE2026 signed package and later Control 24 traceability materials
control24.principalProvisionalHypothesis: resolution-specific and omission/supervision criminal relevance, including possible judicial prevarication only if the strict statutory elements are proved
control24.proceduralBoundary: Control 24 remains autonomous from Control 22 and from private-actor complaints. No criminal case number is invented in this dataset.

privateActors.rule: Private-actor complaints and NEXUS materials may provide connected knowledge/evidence but are not automatically accumulated into Control 22 or Control 24.

method.chain: act → authority → notice/knowledge → decision/omission → execution/non-neutralisation → beneficiary effect → patrimonial consequence → corrective opportunity → later persistence
method.maximumHypothesisRule: Test the strongest legally coherent culpability theory supported by the record, then preserve the strongest innocent/procedural alternative and every missing bridge.

legalFramework.framework: Historical Ley Concursal duties of diligence, loyal representation, estate conservation/administration and judicial supervision; possible CP art. 252 relevance only if entrusted powers, breach/excess, patrimonial damage, causation and the required subjective element are proved.

Possible CP arts. 446-449 relevance is resolution/omission specific and requires the statutory threshold; adverse rulings, deference to an insolvency administrator or failure to adopt the complainant's preferred measure do not themselves establish prevarication or malicious delay.
Possible author/co-author/inducer/cooperator/accomplice theories require knowing participation meeting the applicable Penal Code elements. Repeated benefit alone is not enough.

Conspiracy/concert theories require independent evidence of agreement and resolved criminal purpose where legally punishable. Functional convergence or repeated aligned effects are investigative indicia, not proof of agreement.

unitaryChronology.event: LPB-side quantified banking dispute and warning material reached the insolvency-administration perimeter.
unitaryChronology.significance: Predates the PH122→CAM assignment and weakens any reconstruction that starts only with the June 2018 takeover.

unitaryChronology.event: PH122 assigned the identified mortgage-credit position to CAM.
unitaryChronology.significance: CAM entered the creditor position before later control/adjudication phases.

unitaryChronology.event: JPI nº 2 admitted DP 1041/2017 and ordered production of assignment deed/economics after finding just cause and legitimate interest; in parallel CAM pursued creditor substitution in the insolvency.
unitaryChronology.significance: Two legally distinct routes emerged from the same assignment: LPB information/optionality and CAM creditor recognition.

unitaryChronology.event: The insolvency administration reported favourably on CAM's creditor substitution.
unitaryChronology.significance: The AC became a material validating node in the CAM-recognition route.

unitaryChronology.event: Commercial Court order partially corrected amounts for LPB, rejected LPB's litigious-credit theory, recognised CAM as assignee creditor and expressly relied on favourable AC verification rather than requiring all title documentation sought by LPB.
unitaryChronology.significance: Earliest currently canonical example of active/passive CAM-favourable institutional effect combined with a real LPB-favourable counterpoint.

unitaryChronology.event: The Control 22 source records that a criminal complaint concerning CAM/JDAM existed before the 7 June 2018 access/control event.
unitaryChronology.significance: Potential prior notice is relevant to knowledge and precaution analysis; the complaint itself is an allegation, not proof of wrongdoing.

unitaryChronology.event: Material access/control event at Sun Park.
unitaryChronology.significance: Control 22 asks what the AC knew, authorised, reported, tolerated or failed to delimit/protect and what estate consequences followed.

unitaryChronology.event: Judicial suspension order affecting realisation of specified assets pending appeal.
unitaryChronology.significance: Creates a concrete supervision/neutralisation node for separating AC conduct from judicial conduct.

unitaryChronology.event: Material transaction/disposition episode later subject to non-convalidation.
unitaryChronology.significance: Requires tracing title, possession, accounting, consideration and later corrective action.
The unitary test shifts from whether the earlier operation was validated to whether its factual/patrimonial effects were actually neutralised or restored.

unitaryChronology.event: Competition/alternative-bid and neutral-access/evaluation issues arose in the liquidation trajectory.
unitaryChronology.significance: Tests whether earlier control/information asymmetries affected later competition and realisation value.
Potential convergence point for credit recognition, asset realisation, accounting and difficult-to-reverse external title effects.

unitaryChronology.event: HNT/MYND/RICPE and public-finance/operation layers developed downstream.
unitaryChronology.significance: May evidence consequence/benefit continuity; does not retroactively prove earlier knowledge, agreement or criminal purpose.

maximumInvestigativeHypotheses.actor: Francisco de Borja Rodríguez-Batllori Laffitte / insolvency administration
maximumInvestigativeHypotheses.hypothesis: If the remaining knowledge, authority, damage and subjective-element bridges are proved, the record is capable of supporting an investigation into whether entrusted insolvency-administration powers were repeatedly exercised, withheld or left uncorrected in a way incompatible with loyal estate administration and materially favourable to the CAM-centred beneficiary perimeter.
whyCeilingMoved: The chronology now begins before June 2018 and includes the 2017-2018 credit/retracto recognition asymmetry.
AC favourable verification became an express judicial foundation for CAM creditor recognition.
The current record has not located a measurable LPB estate benefit corresponding to loss of the DP 1041 information/optionality route.
Later control, non-convalidation, competition and adjudication episodes can now be tested as continuity rather than isolated events.
proofNeededForCriminalPromotion: exact entrusted power or duty for each act/omission
documented knowledge at the relevant time
specific breach/excess or knowing failure to exercise a required/protective power
quantified patrimonial damage or loss of estate value/right
causal link between conduct and harm
subjective element required by the offence
exclusion or rebuttal of a rational estate-benefit explanation

maximumInvestigativeHypotheses.hypothesis: If exact knowledge, applicable duty/power, objectively unjust resolution/omission and the statutory subjective threshold are proved act by act, the record is capable of supporting investigation into whether selective judicial intervention, deference to AC verification and later non-neutralisation repeatedly preserved CAM-favourable outcomes despite known LPB protection issues.
maximumInvestigativeHypotheses.counterRecord: The 15 February 2018 order corrected amounts in LPB's favour, and judicial reliance on the AC can be lawful. This prevents a simplistic 'every ruling favoured CAM' narrative.
proofNeededForCriminalPromotion: complete record before the judge at that time
applicable legal duty/power and legally available alternatives
knowledge, grave negligence or malicious delay threshold as applicable
treatment of contrary rulings and legitimate reliance on the AC

maximumInvestigativeHypotheses.actor: Construcciones Acosta Matos / CAM-centred beneficiary perimeter
maximumInvestigativeHypotheses.hypothesis: CAM is repeatedly positioned as beneficiary of creditor recognition, material-control leverage, later realisation/adjudication and downstream operational/title structures. That continuity supports investigation of knowledge and participation; benefit alone does not establish co-authorship, inducement, cooperation or agreement.

maximumInvestigativeHypotheses.actor: AC + judge, jointly in effect, with CAM as recurring beneficiary
maximumInvestigativeHypotheses.hypothesis: Across distinct procedural stages, AC acts/recommendations/omissions and judicial decisions/deference/non-neutralisation repeatedly converged on preserving or strengthening the CAM-centred beneficiary position while LPB lost information, options, control, competitive neutrality or recovery leverage, without a corresponding estate benefit currently identified. This pattern warrants testing for concerted facilitation but does not itself prove agreement or criminal collaboration.

Repeated aligned effects create optics and investigative reasons to test communications, instructions, knowledge-sharing and agreement. Current sources do not independently prove a criminal agreement or resolved joint criminal purpose.

strongestInnocentOrProceduralAlternative: The AC may have reasonably relied on court orders and exercised permissible insolvency discretion.
The judge may have lawfully relied on the AC's verification and resolved legally distinct applications under different standards.
The Article 1535 theory may have been legally weak under a strict concept of litigious credit.
The 15 February 2018 order did correct some figures in LPB's favour.
A complex fragmented hotel/insolvency can generate repeated disputes and asymmetric outcomes without criminal agreement.
A contemporaneous estate-benefit analysis, restoration act, challenge or reconciliation document may exist but remain outside the current corpus.
CAM may have pursued its own legal/economic interests without knowing participation in any breach by public or insolvency actors.
